rationale:
Issue #61 reports that integer 'sub' claims cause problems in JWT parsing. The production fix converts integer 'sub' values to strings while preserving string values. The curator-written trigger test validates both integer-to-string conversion ('123456789') and string preservation ('user-42'), which directly exercises the defect behavior. The minimized patch is identical to the original commit and production-fix patches, containing only the type-check and conversion logic for the 'subject' field with no formatting, refactoring, or unrelated changes. All strict runtime gates passed: trigger is deterministic, buggy version reproduces only the trigger test, fixed version passes all tests, and the differential behavior is confirmed across 32 matrix runs with 3 repetitions. No duplicate root causes exist in the active registry for this project.

All acceptance criteria are satisfied with clear evidence: (1) Issue #61, PR #62, and the production fix all address the same defect—when the JWT 'sub' claim is an integer, it must be converted to a string since the subject field is typed as String?. The fix commit message 'Fixed Issue #61' and PR body explicitly reference the issue. (2) The minimized production patch is identical to the original commit patch and contains only the type-checking logic to convert integer subjects to strings—no formatting, refactoring, documentation, configuration, or test changes. (3) The curator-written trigger test validates the exact defect behavior: an integer subject (123456789) should be parsed and accessible as a string ('123456789'). This is semantically equivalent to the reported defect and does not depend on new APIs introduced by the fix—it uses existing JWT constructor, sign, and tryVerify methods. (4) active_same_project_root_causes is empty, confirming no duplicates exist in the registry.
